document.h: Cover Letter – Fullstack Software Engineer (x/f/m) – AI Health Assistant (Mo) – Alan

section.p: I am writing to apply for the Fullstack Software Engineer position on Alan’s Mo team. Your ambition to build a reliable, safe, and scalable LLM-based health companion strongly resonates with my recent work integrating generative AI into production-oriented systems, and with my long-standing focus on robust backend engineering, interoperability, and high-quality user-facing delivery.

I am a senior software engineer and solutions architect with 25+ years of experience building and operating business-critical services: high-traffic web platforms, integration layers, and data-centric systems. Over the past year, my work has focused on applied generative AI in engineering contexts: integrating LLM APIs into multi-step workflows, constraining outputs using formal schemas (XML/XSD, JSON Schema), and implementing deterministic validation, explicit failure modes, and observability so that AI-powered features remain maintainable and trustworthy in production.

Concretely, I designed and implemented an API workflow orchestration engine (tchatapi.org) in Ballerina to execute complex multi-step scenarios with typed request models, response memory, conditional branching, and reproducible execution via CLI and OpenAPI/Swagger UI. Within this engine, I integrated the OpenAI API as a managed request type so AI-assisted steps can be composed safely alongside traditional API calls, with controlled context injection and validation-oriented execution. This directly aligns with the kind of engineering required to embed an LLM-based assistant into a broader product ecosystem while keeping latency, error recovery, and reliability front and center.

I am also motivated by healthcare itself. Several members of my close family work in healthcare, and during earlier work on health-related systems (HL7 XML workflows), I had the opportunity to collaborate with doctors, professors, researchers, and nurses. That experience made the impact very tangible: enabling healthcare professionals with better tools and more reliable systems improves outcomes and day-to-day care. I am keen to bring the same sense of responsibility to Mo, especially where safety, traceability, and quality are critical.

I value product-minded engineering: building delightful experiences, measuring what matters, and iterating fast without compromising quality. I am comfortable in cross-functional environments, enjoy writing and maintaining clear technical documentation, and I regularly contribute through code reviews and mentoring. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in backend engineering, integration, and production-grade LLM orchestration could contribute to Mo’s next growth phase.

Yours sincerely,
Franck Delahaye
